summary: Task 12 implements design B correctly. The split loop and tolerantDecode find an escaped credential in every quote segment, the head, and the tail without JSON.parse, without a depth ceiling, and without dropping a segment. Both provider callers keep secretFindings before decodedAnswerFindings and check before every write. T129-T138 assert real provider-boundary behavior: they run in the worker, inspect the ledger and file tree, assert the refusal suffix and pattern name, parse labeled integers, and pair every hostile case with a safe twin. The five mutations each fail their named test, and the gate, tsc, and cost-label evidence in the plan all match the recorded logs. No new malformed-string finding and no correctness finding remains. Review B's RB7-01 (api-key-prefix word boundary) is class Other and already recorded there; I do not re-raise it.

Split correctness: the loop runs index 0..text.length inclusive, so the head, every segment between consecutive unescaped quotes, and the tail are each emitted as a segment. The escape flag toggles once per backslash, which keeps \" quote-unescaped and \\\" quote-escaped as JSON does. The tail always decodes, so an unterminated token (T129), a trailing backslash (T130), a raw control char (T131), an invalid escape (T132), and a stray prose quote (T133) each reach the decoder.

tolerantDecode correctness: it resolves \uXXXX (both hex cases), surrogate pairs, and the seven single-character escapes \" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t. It keeps an invalid escape, a lone backslash, and a raw control character as literal text. It is iterative and never throws. The scan resets rule.regex.lastIndex to 0 before each test, so the shared rule objects cannot skip a later segment.

Next layers: a decoded segment that holds a quote goes onto the worklist and is split and decoded again; a decoded segment without a quote is scanned only. This is why the T131 MiniMax envelope (a valid JSON envelope string-encoding the malformed answer) is found: layer 1 decodes the envelope to the inner text, layer 2 decodes the inner \uXXXX to the credential. The two-layer trace was confirmed by reading the code.

Cost and ceiling: the worklist replaces recursion, so a hostile depth returns findings or empty and never raises RangeError. No path decodes a whole layer without segment boundaries. tolerantDecode returns the segment unchanged when no backslash is present, so the T136 wide answer costs one pass only.

Callers keep order and contract: MiniMax calls secretFindings at book-pictures.ts:3401 then decodedAnswerFindings at 3409 inside the paid callback, before the raw copy at 3452 and the review write. Kimi calls readRawAnswer at 3722, secretFindings at 3723, and decodedAnswerFindings at 3732, all before parseModelReview at 3739 and before any write. The task 10 refusal suffix 'the raw answer is refused; no review or raw copy is written.' is byte-identical in both paths. No other production caller of decodedAnswerFindings or secretFindings exists outside book-pictures.ts.

Test meaning: expectMalformedRefusal asserts no timeout, no RangeError, a refusal that names api-key-prefix, no matched secret text, the task 10 suffix, no success ledger entry, no review or raw copies, and byte-identical Kimi snapshots. assertNoSyntheticValues reads real file bytes. T134 and T138 count real finding sets from the worker report; T136 and T137 assert real durations against the 60000 ms and 20000 ms bounds.

A3/A4/A5 review: the time and count assertions parse labeled integers (for example /^wide scan ms:s*([0-9]+)$/ and /^generated findings:s*([0-9]+)$/), not bare digits. Every hostile row pairs with a safe twin (T138: twin cases 245, twin findings 0). No test passes on a missing deliverable: T134 requires 240 findings and 0 twin findings, and a no-op scan yields 0 findings.
